narrative.overview: The whole site behaves like a figure study on paper: warm paper white, warm near-black ink, and one continuous drawn line (--kreska) that rises out of the page rule to become a reclining figure — the classic ATM lesson position — and returns to being a rule. Everything else is reading matter set in a single serif family at a single narrow measure. The world deliberately refuses the practitioner-site default: no pastel hero, no CTA buttons, no card grids, no urgency chips. Reading and finding replace persuading. Color is almost entirely achromatic. The one accent, a sanguine red-chalk (--akcent), is reserved for links and live markers — the things a hand would touch or a teacher would circle. Photography is grayscale, so images live in the same ink-on-paper material as the type and the drawn line. Depth, elevation, and motion are all near-zero: the page is flat, still, and structured by hairline rules.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-and-ink palette with a single sanguine accent, used only where something is interactive or alive
One type family (Literata, optical axis) carrying the entire hierarchy via size, weight, and italic
One narrow reading column (44rem) — no grids, no cards, no sidebars
Two line weights only: the 2.25px drawn stroke (expressive) and 1px hairlines (structural)
Grayscale photography; flat surfaces; a single load-time drawing animation as the only motion

rules.name: The Sanguine Rule
rules.body: The accent appears only on links and live markers (status text, focus, selection). It is never a surface, never a heading color, never decoration. If a new element wants sanguine, ask whether it is interactive or carrying live information; if not, it stays ink.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Prose speaks in two voices only: Ink for what the visitor came to read, Ink Soft for everything supporting it. No grays are invented between them.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every glyph on the site is Literata. Hierarchy comes from optical size, weight (400/450/500/600), and italic — never from a second family, uppercase, or tracking.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No kickers, eyebrows, or small-caps section labels anywhere. A section is introduced by its h2 and nothing above it.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: No box-shadows, no overlays, no fixed or sticky elements, and never backdrop-filter (it froze Chrome's compositor on fixed nav in a prior build — see PRODUCT.md). If an element seems to need elevation, it belongs in the flow instead.

rules.name: The One Stroke Rule
rules.body: --kreska (2.25px) is the only weight for expressive drawn SVG lines. Any new drawn mark uses it exactly; anything structural is a 1px hairline. A third line weight does not exist.

dos: Do set everything in Literata Variable; make hierarchy with optical size, weight (400–600), and italic only.
Do keep all content inside the single 44rem .wrap column and open new sections with a 1px hairline (.sekcja-krecha).
Do style every call to action as a text link (sanguine underline, hover sanguine); the quiet .cichy-link variant is for structural navigation only.
Do render photos with filter: grayscale(1) contrast(1.04) and 2px radius, always.
Do use --kreska (2.25px, round caps) for any drawn SVG mark and 1px --linia for any structural rule — nothing in between.
Do show status text only when it carries live information, and set it in sanguine italic.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: the drawn figure appears pre-drawn; smooth scroll turns off.
donts: Don't add buttons, cards, chips, badges, pastel surfaces, or urgency UI — the world refuses the practitioner-site default.
Don't use sanguine as a background, heading color, or decoration; it belongs to links and live markers only.
Don't add kickers, eyebrows, uppercase labels, or letterspaced small caps.
Don't use shadows, fixed/sticky positioning, or backdrop-filter anywhere (documented Chrome compositor freeze on fixed elements).
Don't add scroll-triggered reveal animations; the figure drawing itself once on load is the only motion in the world.
Don't introduce a second font family, a second accent color, or a third line weight.
